newsitem.title: UK: UK MP into hiding, another standing down.
newsitem.headline: UK MP into hiding, another standing down.

text.p: Beleaguered Prime Minister John Major's election campaign was overshadowed on Friday by sex and sleaze allegations that have persistently bedevilled the ruling Conservative party.

Conservative member of parliament Piers Merchant, accused of having an affair with a 17-year-old nightclub hostess, went into hiding over Easter as pressure mounted for him to step down as a candidate before the May 1 election.

Then the two main opposition parties contemplated fielding a joint "anti-sleaze candidate" against Conservative former minister Neil Hamilton, embroiled in a row about taking cash to raise questions in parliament. He denies the allegations.

The opposition Labour Party, overwhelming opinion poll favourite to end 18 years of Conservative rule, said John Kelly, its candidate against Hamilton, would step down in a bid to force the Conservative to do the same.
Labour could then possibly cooperate with the centrist Liberal Democrats in fielding an "anti-corruption, pro-public standards" candidate. The Conservatives called the ploy "a pathetic gimmick".

As the Easter weekend turned into one of suffering for the Conservatives, party chairman Brian Mawhinney urged Merchant's local constituency to make up its mind soon on his candidature after the sex allegations.
"I hope that meeting is called quickly and that we can move onto the substantive issues which will determine the outcome of this election campaign," he told BBC Radio.

The Conservatives, buoyed by low inflation, falling unemployment and a strong economy, had hoped to concentrate their fire on the opposition Labour Party's links with the trade unions. But sleaze has dominated the headlines.
On Wednesday, former junior minister Tim Smith stood down as a candidate over his failure to declare that he accepted cash for asking questions in parliament.
Then the tabloid Sun, which had declared its support for Labour, printed photographs showing the married Merchant kissing blonde teenager Anna Cox. Merchant denied the story.
The local party chiefs in his southern England constituency of Beckenham, a Conservative stronghold, has summoned him for questioning on Tuesday after the Easter weekend break.
To add to the woes of the Conservatives, former government minister Allan Stewart was taken to hospital on Thursday suffering from a nervous breakdown, party officials said.
He had agreed to step down as a parliamentary candidate on Tuesday after press reports linked him to a married woman he is said to have met while attending a clinic specialising in alchohol problems.
But the latest opinion poll did offer some comfort to the Conservatives, who under Prime Minister John Major are bidding to win their fifth election victory in a row.

The Independent newspaper poll showed Labour's huge lead has fallen by three points. But the Conservatives are still 24 points behind Labour, revived by centrist Tony Blair after ditching much of the party's socialist dogma.
